extraction.name: TextVQA
extraction.description: A dataset for visual question answering containing questions that require reading and reasoning about text in images. It contains 45,336 questions on 28,408 images, with 10 human-provided answers for each question-image pair.
extraction.creator: Amanpreet Singh, Vivek Natarajan, Meet Shah, Yu Jiang, Xinlei Chen, Dhruv Batra, Devi Parikh, Marcus Rohrbach
extraction.citeAs: Singh, A., Natarajan, V., Shah, M., Jiang, Y., Chen, X., Batra, D., Parikh, D., & Rohrbach, M. (2019). Towards VQA Models That Can Read.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was collected from Open Images v3 using a three-stage crowdsourcing pipeline. First, annotators identified images that did not contain text using a forced-choice yes/no flag, and those images were filtered out. Second, annotators were shown an image and asked to provide 1-2 questions that require reading the text in the image to answer; for the second question, they were shown the first question and asked to create a different question with a different answer. Third, following VQA and VizWiz, 10 answers were collected for each question. Additional quality control included flags for no text in image, not a question, answering does not require reading text, and unanswerable; questions with majority worker flags were removed. Hand-crafted questions with known answers were also used to identify and filter bad annotators.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: In some cases, when the OCR system was unable to detect text, images had 0 OCR tokens; these cases were restricted to about 1.5k images and the authors manually verified that the images actually do contain text.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images were sourced from the Open Images v3 dataset. Categories likely to contain text were identified by sampling 100 random images from each category (or all images if fewer than 100), running the Rosetta OCR model on them, computing the average number of OCR boxes per category, normalizing these averages, and using them as per-category weights for sampling images.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Training and validation images were collected from the Open Images training set, and test images were collected from the Open Images test set.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The authors filtered out images identified as not containing text and removed noisy data from annotators. They also removed questions where a majority of workers marked any of the quality-control flags: no text in image, not a question, answering the question does not require reading text in image, or unanswerable.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: To identify image categories likely to contain text, the authors ran Rosetta OCR on sampled Open Images categories and used the average number of OCR boxes per category as normalized sampling weights. During dataset creation, images without text and low-quality annotations were filtered out.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators were asked to write questions such that answering them requires reading text in the image; they were explicitly instructed that it is acceptable if the answer cannot be directly copied from the text but must be inferred or paraphrased. A second distinct question with a different answer was collected for some images. For each question, 10 answers were collected from humans. Annotators were also given quality-control options to flag problematic items.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper reports agreement statistics for answers: all 10 annotators agree on the most common answer for 22.8% of questions, while 3 or more annotators agree on the most common answer for 97.9% of questions.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper motivates the dataset by noting that questions requiring reading text in images are frequently asked by visually impaired users of assistive devices, and states that this skill is important for applications involving aiding visually impaired users.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper states that the dataset does not have significant biases with respect to images and questions, based on low performance of question-only and image-only baselines. It also notes a model bias where LoRRA often answers city-related questions with "new york."
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The effective OCR upper bound is limited by OCR quality. The OCR model still fails at detecting text that is rotated, unstructured such as scribbles, or partially occluded. The model can only copy a single OCR token, while 8.9% of TextVQA questions can only be answered by combining multiple OCR tokens. The paper also notes a large gap between model and human performance.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is introduced to facilitate research and benchmarking on visual question answering that requires reading and reasoning about text in images. The paper defines train, validation, and test splits of sizes 34,602, 5,000, and 5,734 respectively, and uses the dataset to train and evaluate VQA models such as LoRRA.
